cohort: 2573 mothers who delivered at two comprehensive emergency obstetric care service facilities in Ngora district, Eastern Uganda, between April 2018 and March 2019
finding: The study found that the caesarean section rate was 14%, with the main indications being obstructed labour, fetal distress, big baby, and cephalopelvic disproportion.
mod_finding: While caesarean section was viewed positively by some as a life-saving intervention, others held negative perceptions, considering it a curse, marriage-breaker, misfortune, money-maker, a sign of incompetent health workers, and being for lazy or wealthy women.
